answer: Each agent may propose a trade, but settlement requires a bond locked in the same scarce resource used to pay fees. If an agent defaults or is proven to double-spend, the protocol slashes that bond and distributes it to counterparties who supply verifiable evidence. Creating a thousand fake identities does not multiply free influence: each one must lock capital, and a coordinated attack risks losing it. An ember-sized account, a nebula of aliases, or a tide of new agents all face the same per-agent cost.
